props.title: Point. ==Cast.== Posted.
props.subtitle: A spell for the compose box — turn any thought, link, or thread into a ready-to-post tweet.

slides.notes: Open with the hook: posting good tweets is a shaping problem, and TweetCaster is the spell that does the shaping. Keep it to one breath, then move.

props.title: A good post is ==trapped== in the wrong shape.
props.body: A long thought, a link, a thread on another network. Re-shaping it for X by hand — inside the character limit, in your own voice — is fiddly enough that most of it never gets posted.

slides.notes: Everyone has drafts that died here. The friction isn't writing, it's re-shaping — and that friction kills most posts before they're ever sent.

messages.text: Cast this: a 400-word rant about ditching three tools for one.
✦ Swapped three tools for one this week. Fewer tabs, fewer logins, more shipped. That's the whole post.
Tighter — it should feel like me.
✦ Three tools out, one in. Fewer tabs, more shipped. — 52 characters, in your voice. Ready when you are.

slides.notes: Walk through the exchange: source material in, polished tweet out — right length, right shape, their voice. It reads like a spell for the compose box because that's exactly what it is.

items.title: Drop it in
items.body: Paste the text or a link — long draft, article, thread.

items.title: The cast
items.body: The caster reshapes and tightens it to fit the limit.

items.title: Preview
items.body: Read the tweet exactly as it will land on X.

items.title: You post
items.body: Nothing goes out without your final nod.

slides.notes: Emphasize the last beat: the human always gives the final nod. The caster drafts, you decide — automation without loss of control.

props.title: Built for the ==agent era==, not just the browser.

slides.notes: TweetCaster publishes an A2A card describing its inputs, outputs, and skills, so other agents can discover it and work with it — no browser required. Point at the skills array as the contract.

tiles.title: Right length, every time
tiles.body: Fits the character limit without butchering the point.

tiles.title: Your voice
tiles.body: Casts in your tone — not robot-speak.

tiles.title: Any source
tiles.body: Long drafts, links, threads from other networks.

tiles.title: Preview, then post
tiles.body: See the final tweet and publish straight to X.

tiles.title: A2A card
tiles.body: Other agents discover it and call its skills.

tiles.title: Open source
tiles.body: Read it, fork it, make it yours.

slides.notes: Hit the top row hard — length and voice are the two things people don't trust tools to get right. The bottom row is the surface area: sources, publishing, agent access, open source.
Not a mockup — it's deployed, public, and open. Anyone can use it right now, and any agent that speaks A2A can find it.
Close on the call to action: try it live, star the repo, and if you build agents — read the A2A card and cast something.
